To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lung is susceptible to injury from inhaled mitogens, and that the severity of such injury is governed by the mitogenic potency of the agent in question, the dose of agent inhaled, the duration of exposure, and the degree of immunological responsiveness to the agent in question.
the lung is subject to parenchymal inflammation and injury by inhaled mitogens, and that this injury is potentiated by the simultaneous presence of inhaled antigen.

inhaled mitogenic agents are highly effective in inducing pulmonary inflammatory reactions, whereas inhaled antigen (lacking mitogen activity) produce little or no parenchymal inflammation in immunized recipients.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanisms of lung injury produced by inhaled antigens, and by inhaled mitogens, which act as nonspecific polyclonal activators of the lung's own immune effector systems, thereby inducing inflammatory reactions which can lead to parenchymal damage.

the immunologic basis for parenchymal pulmonary inflammation induced by inhaled environmental antigens and other agents, and with the mediators and biochemical mechanisms which regulate this response.
the mechanisms whereby environmental agents injure lung tissues and the biochemical basis of individual susceptibility to such injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lung is susceptible to injury in a number of different ways by a variety of different environmental agents.
the immunologic mechanisms of parenchy- mal lung injury are not fully understood.
the immunological mechanisms of parenchmal lung injury are not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the immune system is involved in a wide range of lung disorders.
the lung is a very susceptible organ to injury by a wide variety of environmental agents.

the lung is susceptible to injury from circulating immune complexes, humoral autoantbodies and immune lymphocytes, and inhaled environmental agents (mitogens) which trigger nonspecific inflammatory reactions in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two different types of lung inflammation.
the lung is a target for the immune system, and it can be injured by the immune system.
the immune system is very complex, and that the immune system can actually cause damage to itself.
